question:
Match the following. 

 
 

 
 
(i)

 
 Gir National Park 
 
 
(a)

 
 
 
Rhinos

 
 
 

 
 
(ii)

 
 Rajaji National Park

options.text: i - d, ii - b, iii - c, iv - a
i - d, ii - c, iii - a, iv - b
i - c, ii - d, iii - b, iv - a
i - a, ii - b, iii - c, iv - d

solution:
The correct anser is __**option 3.**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gir National Park **

 
 
• **Indian Lions or Asiatic lion is one of the five big cat **species, found in India,
 
• A single population exists in the **Gir National Park of Gujarat state**.
 
• The scientific name of the Asiatic lion is **Panthera Leo Persica**.
 
• It is listed as **endangered **species under the red list in the IUCN list.
 
 
 
• Rajaji National National Park, most famous for its elephant population.
 
 
• Located at the Himalayan foothills, near Haridwar, Rishikesh and Dehradun, with Ganga and Song rivers, flowing through it.
 
• In 1983, three sanctuaries in Uttarakhand - Rajaji, Motichur and Chilla - were amalgamated into a large protected area and named Rajaji National Park.
 
• This area is the north-western limit of Asian elephants. 
 
 
 
• **Keoladeo National Park **
 
 
• **It **is located in the Bharatpur district of Rajasthan. It is formerly known as the Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary.
 
• This site was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985.
 
 
 
• **Kaziranga National Park **
 
 
• It is located in **Assam**.
 
• It is famous for **one-horned Rhinoceros.**
 
• It is located in Golaghat and Nagaon, in the **Karbi Anglong district **of Assam in northeast India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Park:**

 
 
• There are 106 National parks in India.
 
• First national park in India- **Ramganga National Park (**Jim Corbett National Park or Hailey National Park).
 
• No human activity/rights allowed except for the ones permitted by the Chief Wildlife Warden of the State.
